subject: Model shortlist + context & token profile — implementation workplan

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up after demo — context sizes and token volumes

Thanks again for today — the demo was helpful. A few clarifications from our engineering team so we can scope the integration and onboarding: 

1) Typical user flows:
 - Short Q&A (product discovery): avg prompt ~ 120 tokens, expected model output 80–150 tokens.
 - Document-augmented search: user supplies a selected document + query. Documents are generally 3–8k characters (we estimate ~600–1,500 tokens depending on formatting).
 - Batch classification jobs: customers will occasionally run bulk inference (10–20k documents/day) where each doc averages 400 tokens.

2) Volume estimates (starting month): expected active users ~ 2,500, daily queries ~ 18k (mix of short Q&A and doc search). Rough monthly token estimate we get from our side: ~12–18M tokens/mo across types. Peak concurrency concern: internal ops want to be safe for 60–90 RPS during peak marketing events.

3) Constraints: PII in documents is limited to names and account IDs (we cannot retain raw docs for more than 30 days), and we need regional routing to US data centers only.

Can you confirm whether the above shapes your model shortlist and any immediate sizing recs (dedicated vs hosted)? Also attaching a rough CSV with sample counts will help — I'll send the file separately.

Thanks,
James
VP Product, AvaTech
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: James Nolan <james.nolan@avatech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up after demo — context sizes and token volumes

James — great detail, this is exactly what we needed. Quick replies inline, plus a proposed next step (kickoff + technical pre-reads attached):

- Thanks for the volumes. Based on ~12–18M tokens/mo and peak 60–90 RPS, we recommend we'll start with a mixed deployment:
  * Hosted (production reads + light writes) for quick time-to-value while we iterate on prompts and evals
  * Dedicated pool for document-augmented search paths that need consistent latency at scale and to reduce unit cost for heavy document batches

- Context length needs you described (up to ~1,500 tokens typical, occasional 3,000+ tokens for long docs) points to supporting 4k context for the short term and 8k where higher context matters.

- Model shortlist (initial candidates — we'll validate during the eval sprint):
  1) Mistral-instruct-8B (fast, cost-efficient for short Q&A)
  2) Llama-3-13B-8k (good balance for doc-augmented search at 4k context; 8k variant for larger documents)
  3) RedSea-70B-quant (higher-quality generative path reserved for high-value responses — use with sampling controls and fallbacks)

- Serving recommendations (preliminary):
  * Token budgeting per request: plan for 2,000 tokens avg end-to-end (input+output) to be conservative.
  * Batching: enable dynamic batching on the Dedicated pool for doc classification (batch size target 32–64 depending on observed latency).
  * Caching: prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts and embeddings.
  * Quantization: prefer q4_0 for 13B-class models in Dedicated; q8/q4m for larger 70B where acceptable.

Action items:
 - Rishi: can you validate the Dedicated footprint estimate below and confirm whether we should recommend 4 x A100-80GB equiv nodes to start (autoscale rules + burst to 6 nodes)?
 - Marissa: I'll draft the SOW and a phased rollout plan (pilot -> scale -> handoff) and share by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: avatech_token_estimates.csv, model_shortlist_notes.md

Proposed next step: 60-minute kickoff with engineering on Monday 12/7 (I put a tentative slot on your calendar).

—Naomi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On Thu, 03 Dec 2026 at 11:05 Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai> wrote:
> - Rishi: can you validate the Dedicated footprint estimate below and confirm whether we should recommend 4 x A100-80GB equiv nodes to start (autoscale rules + burst to 6 nodes)?

Thanks — quick validation and a couple of clarifying figures from infra:

Summary recommendation (Dedicated pool):
 - Start: 4 x A100-80GB-equivalent with autoscale floor 2 / burst to 6 during scheduled marketing events.
 - Rationale: With average request budget ~2k tokens and peak 80 RPS, continuous batching reduces per-token compute and keeps avg latency < 300 ms for the 13B family.
 - For high-quality fallbacks (70B quantized), keep a small warm pool (1–2 instances) and route only escalations or high-value responses there. Use fallback policy in the Console.

Estimated costs & throughput (rough):
 - 13B q4_0 on Dedicated: ~180–220 tokens/sec per GPU with batching; with 4 GPUs sustained ~72k tokens/sec capacity (headroom for spiky bursts).
 - 70B q4m on Dedicated warm nodes: ~40–70 tokens/sec per GPU.

Monthly token run-rate calc (example):
 - Baseline tokens/mo: 12M tokens -> compute fits comfortably in the Dedicated sizing above with hosted handling low-latency short Q&A.
 - If you hit the higher estimate ~18M tokens/mo, autoscale + caching should keep unit costs within targeted range.

Operational notes:
 - Data retention: set workspace retention to 30 days; we'll enable masked logging for PII fields.
 - Security: US-only routing will be enforced at the routing policy and region tag on the Dedicated pool.

I'll prepare a short runbook for the pilot (warmup, canary, rollback) and share it with the kickoff pack.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
